question: How late can a candidate enter the examination room after the exam has started?
reference_answer: Candidates may be admitted up to thirty minutes after the official start of the examination, and no additional time is given for arriving late.

question: Can I take my mobile phone into the examination room?
reference_answer: No. A mobile phone or any other communication device is not permitted into the examination room; it must be left at the point the Supervisor designates.

question: What is the minimum attendance students must maintain for lectures and tutorials?
reference_answer: Students are generally expected to maintain at least 75% attendance for lectures, tutorials and practical sessions in each module.

question: How many days after an exam do I have to submit an extenuating circumstances claim?
expected_sources: Revision to NSBM EC Guidelines to students from Aug2023.pdf
reference_answer: The EC form with evidence must be submitted no later than 14 working days after the exam date; claims are reviewed by the EC Board.

question: How much is the repeat examination fee for an NSBM degree programme?
reference_answer: A repeat examination or coursework for an NSBM degree (Year 1 to Year 4) costs Rs. 3000, from 2 January 2023.

question: How long do I have to submit repeat coursework after downloading it?
reference_answer: Repeat coursework must be submitted on or before the 14th day after the date it was downloaded from the portal (two weeks).

question: How is GPA calculated at NSBM?
expected_sources: Here are the standard guidelines for calculating your GPA (G (1).pdf
reference_answer: GPA is a credit-weighted average on a 4.00 scale: the sum of (grade point x module credits) divided by the total credits.

question: What is the minimum GPA needed for First Class Honours?
expected_sources: NSBM Degree Programmes_Exam By Laws _ Version 1 (17.2 onwards) _Students.pdf
reference_answer: A minimum GPA of 3.7, with no grade below C at the first attempt and an A or better in at least half of the courses, completed within four academic years.

question: What overall mark is needed to pass a module?
reference_answer: Students typically need an overall final mark of at least 50%, combining continuous assessment and exam marks.

question: On what grounds can I appeal my examination results?
reference_answer: Appeals are considered for administrative or clerical errors, documented extenuating circumstances, or procedural irregularities in how the assessment was conducted.

question: What A/L results do I need to enter an undergraduate programme?
reference_answer: Usually 3 simple passes (S) or better in the G.C.E. Advanced Level in a single attempt, or completion of an approved foundation programme.

question: What qualifications does Mr. Gayan Perera have?
reference_answer: Master of Business Analytics (Data Science), University of Colombo; MSc Computer Science, Staffordshire University; BSc (Hons) Management Information Systems, NSBM.

question: Is poor internet connectivity accepted as an extenuating circumstance?
expected_sources: Revision to NSBM EC Guidelines to students from Aug2023.pdf
reference_answer: No. Poor internet connectivity is listed among the problems that will not be approved as extenuating circumstances.

question: In which months does NSBM take in new undergraduate students?
reference_answer: NSBM typically has three intakes a year, in February, June and October; each intake follows its own semester schedule.
